landscape.questionsSubheader: Expand and simplify — show your working in your workbook

intro.note: To expand double brackets, multiply every term in the first bracket by every term in the second bracket. You can use the FOIL method (First, Outside, Inside, Last) or the grid method to organise your working. Then collect like terms to simplify.

visual.title: Visual aid — grid method
visual.caption: Each cell shows the product of its row and column headers: (x+2)(x+3) = x² + 5x + 6.

params.aria: Grid model showing (x+2)(x+3): top row x times x gives x squared, x times +3 gives 3x; bottom row +2 times x gives 2x, +2 times +3 gives 6. Collecting like terms: x squared + 3x + 2x + 6 = x squared + 5x + 6.

methodSteps: 1  Multiply each term in the first bracket by each term in the second
2  Write each product in its grid cell
3  Collect like terms (the two middle terms)
commonMistakes: Forgetting the last term: you must multiply the constant in the first bracket by the constant in the second.
Sign errors with negatives: remember that a negative times a negative gives a positive.
Writing x + x instead of 2x for the middle term when collecting like terms.
Forgetting that x × x = x², not 2x.
workedExample: Step 1 — Draw the grid with (x + 2) down the side and (x + 3) along the top.
Step 2 — Fill in: x·x = x²,  x·3 = 3x,  2·x = 2x,  2·3 = 6

intro.objective: Expand products of two binomials (double brackets) using the grid method or FOIL. Collect like terms to write a simplified quadratic expression.
commonMistakes: Forgetting the last term: you must multiply the constant in the first bracket by the constant in the second.
Sign errors with negatives: remember that a negative times a negative gives a positive.
Writing x + x instead of 2x for the middle term when collecting like terms.
Forgetting that x × x = x², not 2x.
methodSteps: Step 1: Draw a grid with the terms of the first bracket down the left and the terms of the second bracket along the top.
Step 2: Fill in each cell by multiplying the row header by the column header.
Step 3: Write out all four products in a line.
Step 4: Collect like terms (the two middle terms will usually be alike).
Step 5: Check by substituting a simple value such as x = 10.
workedExample: Step 1 — Draw the grid: columns are x and +3, rows are x and +2.
Step 2 — Fill in: x·x = x²,  x·3 = 3x,  2·x = 2x,  2·3 = 6

frame: Draw a 2×2 grid. Put x and +1 down the left side, x and +2 along the top.
Fill in each cell: x·x, x·2, 1·x, 1·2.
Write all four terms, then collect the like terms together.
Draw a 2×2 grid. Put x and +3 down the left side, x and +4 along the top.
Fill in each cell by multiplying the row term by the column term.
Add up the four products and collect like terms.
